data.title: Stabilize WebGL in Android simulator Chrome

data.body: Implemented Chrome 113 WebGL launch preparation: exact goog:chromeOptions flags, safe debug-app ownership and cleanup, booted-AVD doctor diagnostics, evidence metadata, self-tests, docs, and an interaction-reset scroll correction. Validation: self-test, Android doctor, typecheck, 157 Vitest tests, and build pass. Focused S24-class run confirmed WebGL Hero and native drag; final tap initially exposed retained scroll (corrected). Immediate rerun was interrupted by the already-booted emulator process exiting before the first route, an external host resource failure.

Independent cold review of commit 2d680cc: implementation-level rework/validation needed before completion. Code inspection passes the core design: the workaround is declared only on the two maintained Android profiles, gated to exact Chrome major 113, supplies exactly --in-process-gpu/--disable-vulkan/--ignore-gpu-blocklist through goog:chromeOptions.args, leaves iOS/newer Chrome unchanged, diagnoses conflicting debug_app/wait_for_debugger state read-only, preserves compatible pre-existing Chrome state, clears only runner-owned state, rolls back setup after force-stop failure, and performs cleanup from the runner failure path. Existing browser-log, runtime-health, Hero readiness, label safe-zone, native drag/tap, route, and orientation assertions remain mandatory; the only suite adjustment resets retained scroll before the native interaction. Self-tests/docs cover gating, capability shape, conflicts, ownership, idempotent cleanup, and emulator-vs-physical scope. Review validation: pnpm simulators:self-test PASS (required unsandboxed macOS Mach-port access), pnpm typecheck PASS, pnpm test PASS (157/157), pnpm build PASS. Read-only Android doctor correctly reported Chrome 113 workaround required with pre-existing-compatible debug state; it exited nonzero only because ports 4173 and 4723 were already occupied. Acceptance evidence is not complete: 2026-07-23T18-36-25-213Z proves route health, Hero WebGL readiness, mobile menu, Story CTA, and native WebGL drag, but the S24-class run failed on native node tap; the scroll-reset correction has not completed a full rerun because 2026-07-23T18-38-36-884Z lost the emulator/DevTools session, and no android-emulator-tablet passing manifest exists. Rerun the focused S24-class profile to a complete passing manifest, then the tablet profile, without weakening assertions; re-review can then mark done.

Review follow-up on new evidence test-results/mobile-simulators/2026-07-23T18-42-02-738Z: this is a harness false-positive and confirms implementation-level rework is needed before completion. The S24-class run passed the shared in-page runtime-health probe on /political-club with zero assetErrors, consoleErrors, fetchFailures, incompleteMedia, pageErrors, or statusFailures. The only failure was three Chrome browser-log entries with source=network and level=SEVERE for a 403 from the external Luma iframe telemetry endpoint o370968.ingest.us.sentry.io; it is neither the Fractal origin nor a first-party resource. Refine browser-log classification so only cross-origin external network-load failures are retained as nonfatal evidence, while first-party network failures and every SEVERE/ERROR JavaScript, console, and page error remain fatal. Record both fatal and external-network classifications in the manifest and add focused self-tests proving external network is evidence-only while same-origin network and all JS/page errors still fail. Then rerun the complete S24-class profile and tablet profile. FRAC-19 remains in review.

Implemented review-cycle classifier rework: only parseable cross-origin HTTP(S) SEVERE/ERROR entries from Chrome's network source are evidence-only; same-origin, relative/unparseable network failures and all non-network SEVERE/ERROR entries remain fatal. Manifests now record fatal and externalNetwork classifications. Focused self-tests mirror the observed external Sentry 403 and prove first-party network plus JavaScript/console/page failures stay fatal. Validation: pnpm simulators:self-test PASS, pnpm typecheck PASS, pnpm test PASS (157/157), git diff --check PASS. No homepage/WebGL/native assertions changed.

S24 host-GPU rerun 2026-07-23T18-49-59-899Z passed all route checks, WebGL readiness, native drag/tap, and CTA navigation to /#story. It then failed because CTA navigation reloaded the document and removed the injected runtime-health listener before the suite reset to /. Implementation-level rework: reinstall/verify runtime-health capture after the expected CTA navigation before beginning the next route; keep all checks fatal.

Review Cycle 2 implementation rework: after the expected Story CTA document navigation, the suite now waits for document completion, reinstalls and verifies the existing runtime-health capture, then resets/begins the next route with all health assertions unchanged. Added a focused self-test proving reload removes the page-global capture and explicit reinstall restores beginRuntimeHealthRoute. Validation: pnpm simulators:self-test PASS (required unsandboxed macOS Mach-port access), pnpm typecheck PASS, node --check scripts/mobile-simulators/suite.mjs PASS, git diff --check PASS.

S24 run 2026-07-23T18-54-40-927Z passed route sweep, browser-chrome transition, WebGL, CTA, health capture recovery, and native drag, then native tap missed Co-Living. Root cause: suite inferred browserTop as total non-web height (340px), incorrectly including Android's 63px bottom navigation bar. Native hierarchy proves Chrome WebView bounds [0,279][1080,2280]. Implementation-level rework: use actual native WebView rect for CSS-to-native coordinate mapping (Android and Apple selectors), with strict fallback/validation and focused pure transform tests.

Review Cycle 3 implementation rework: native interactions now resolve the sole visible platform WebView in NATIVE_APP (android.webkit.WebView / XCUIElementTypeWebView), validate its bounds and per-axis scale against the live CSS visualViewport and native/CSS screen dimensions, and use that rect for both Hero drag and node-tap coordinates. The inaccurate all-non-web-height top-offset heuristic was removed with no fallback. Added pure transform self-tests covering the observed 1080x2340 device, 412.190x762.286 CSS viewport, [0,279][1080,2280] WebView target placement, old-heuristic rejection, and off-viewport rejection. Validation: pnpm simulators:self-test PASS (unsandboxed for macOS Mach ports), pnpm typecheck PASS, syntax checks PASS, git diff --check PASS. All interaction and health assertions remain mandatory.

Final independent review after b71a168: minor inline locator correction applied. Real S24-class evidence 2026-07-23T19-04-39-816Z passed the route sweep and reached native interaction, then correctly exposed that Appium XPath //android.webkit.WebView matched zero elements even though the Android native hierarchy represents the WebView as a generic node with class=android.webkit.WebView. Updated Android to //*[@class="android.webkit.WebView"] and iOS to the corresponding attribute XPath //*[@type="XCUIElementTypeWebView"], with focused exact-selector assertions. Coordinate mapping, WebGL/runtime-health checks, native interaction requirements, and host setup are unchanged. Validation: pnpm simulators:self-test PASS (unsandboxed macOS Mach-port access), pnpm typecheck PASS, syntax checks PASS, git diff --check PASS. Static review finds no further code-level blocker, but acceptance evidence is still incomplete: keep FRAC-19 in review until fresh complete passing manifests exist for both android-emulator-s24-class and android-emulator-tablet.

Follow-up independent review of S24 evidence 2026-07-23T19-09-38-685Z: UiAutomator2's compressed native tree omitted the WebView even with the correct class-attribute XPath. Applied a narrow Android-only fallback using the sole visible Chrome toolbar resource-id com.android.chrome:id/toolbar. The derived viewport starts at toolbar.y + toolbar.height, spans the native window width, and uses live visualViewport.height multiplied by DPR/visual scale only after validating DPR against both native/CSS screen axes, viewport width, toolbar width, and native bounds. The existing WebView transform performs the final per-axis validation; there is no subtraction-heuristic fallback. iOS remains strict WebView lookup. Focused tests cover the observed toolbar [0,132,1080,147] => viewport y=279,height~=2001 and reject invalid toolbar width. Validation: pnpm simulators:self-test PASS, pnpm typecheck PASS, syntax checks PASS, git diff --check PASS. FRAC-19 remains in review pending fresh passing S24-class and tablet manifests.

Follow-up review of S24 evidence 2026-07-23T19-14-19-704Z: the strict Chrome toolbar locator found exactly one visible element, confirming the fallback target, but WebdriverIO v9 elements do not expose getRect(). Replaced rectangle reads for both native WebView and Chrome toolbar paths with one adapter that combines supported getLocation() and getSize() calls into {x,y,width,height}. Added a focused async adapter assertion using the observed toolbar rectangle. Coordinate derivation, validation, interactions, and health assertions are unchanged. Validation: pnpm simulators:self-test PASS, pnpm typecheck PASS, syntax checks PASS, git diff --check PASS. FRAC-19 remains in review pending fresh passing S24-class and tablet manifests.

Inline review fix after exhausted formal cycles: native node taps were aimed at the center of the visible HTML label, but production labels use pointer-events:none and a computed transform (currently translateY(-28px)); the actual R3F hit sphere remains at the Html projection anchor. The suite now captures each post-drag label's live computed DOMMatrix m41/m42 and derives anchor x=centerX-m41, y=centerY-m42 before CSS-to-native mapping, so future translation changes remain accounted for. Single-point native gestures now emit W3C pointerMove -> pointerDown -> pause -> pointerUp; multi-point drag actions retain pointerMove transitions unchanged. Focused self-tests pin both action sequences and the projected-anchor inversion. Validation: pnpm simulators:self-test PASS, pnpm typecheck PASS, syntax checks PASS, git diff --check PASS. No production code, coordinate-space validation, or acceptance assertions changed. FRAC-19 remains in review pending the real S24/tablet evidence.

Inline review fix from tablet evidence 2026-07-23T19-35-01-279Z: Chrome's toolbar collapse is observed through visualViewport even when innerHeight stays fixed. The suite now treats a >4 CSS-pixel live-viewport increase as a real collapse, performs the downward expansion gesture only in that case and while the page remains scrolled, then captures expanded metrics/screenshot before scrolling to top. If no collapse occurs, it skips the pull-to-refresh-prone gesture and records the transition as inconclusive for manual confirmation. Both paths then wait for document readiness, defensively reinstall runtime-health capture, recapture final metrics, and require scrollY approximately zero before subsequent checks. Phone 762->818->762 remains an observed expanded/collapsed/expanded transition. Focused self-tests cover the phone transition, sub-tolerance/no-collapse gating, and inconclusive result. Validation: pnpm simulators:self-test PASS, pnpm typecheck PASS, syntax checks PASS, git diff --check PASS. FRAC-19 remains in review pending rerun evidence.

Final inline reliability fix: both automatic Fractal_Tablet_API_34 boots using the runner's GUI/-gpu auto invocation exited before ADB, while two manual headless host-GPU boots completed and produced full tablet evidence. The production runner now obtains exact Android emulator arguments from one shared config helper for both maintained phone/tablet profiles: -no-window, -gpu host, -no-snapshot-load, -no-snapshot-save, -no-boot-anim, and -cores 2, while preserving each profile's AVD name and emulator port. No -memory flag is emitted because emulator hardware configuration overrides it. Focused self-tests pin the complete argument vector for both Android profiles and reject -memory. Validation: pnpm simulators:self-test PASS, pnpm typecheck PASS, config/run/self-test syntax checks PASS, git diff --check PASS. FRAC-19 remains in review pending root's clean auto-boot tablet verification.

Inline evidence-retention fix: Playwright configured outputDir=test-results, so any Playwright invocation cleaned the parent directory that also contained simulator evidence at test-results/mobile-simulators. Playwright output is now isolated at sibling test-results/playwright. The simulator self-test statically pins the configured outputDir and verifies neither resolved output root contains the other, preventing destructive cleanup overlap in either direction. Validation: pnpm simulators:self-test PASS, pnpm typecheck PASS, syntax and git diff checks PASS. FRAC-19 remains in review while S24/tablet evidence is regenerated under the protected simulator root.

Final independent acceptance review PASS. Retained combined evidence test-results/mobile-simulators/2026-07-23T20-00-52-264Z has run.json result=passed and complete passing manifests for android-emulator-s24-class and android-emulator-tablet. Both are Android 14/API 34, arm64-v8a, Play Store images, Chrome 113.0.5672.136, exact expected physical size/density, and wasAlreadyBooted=false, proving the production runner auto-booted them. Emulator logs show host GPU selection, Apple M1 Pro Vulkan, full cold startup, snapshots disabled, correct 1080x2340/420 and 1600x2560/320 displays, boot completion, and graceful kill handling; post-run adb devices is empty, proving cleanup. Both manifests record the exact --in-process-gpu/--disable-vulkan/--ignore-gpu-blocklist workaround as required with safe pre-existing-compatible debug ownership and no runner-owned cleanup. S24 passed the complete route/redirect sweep, all responsive/runtime-health checks, WebGL Hero readiness, 762->818->762 browser toolbar transition, scroll restoration, mobile menu, Story CTA, native WebGL drag, native Co-Living node tap navigation, browser-log capability, and portrait->landscape without reload. Tablet passed responsive/runtime-health checks, WebGL Hero readiness, 1128->1224->1128 toolbar transition, scroll restoration, browser-log capability, and portrait->landscape without reload. Every route-runtime-health record passed; every browser-log classification has zero fatal entries (three external Luma/Sentry network entries remain evidence-only as designed). Representative portrait/landscape screenshots for both profiles show the Hero, labels, text, CTA, and browser/system chrome contained without clipping. Static review of all eleven FRAC-19 commits against the plan found changes limited to simulator tooling/docs/Playwright output isolation plus Lattice tracking; no production site assertions were weakened. Final validation: pnpm simulators:self-test PASS; pnpm simulators:doctor -- --platform android PASS; pnpm typecheck PASS; pnpm test PASS (160/160); pnpm build PASS; git diff --check PASS. Acceptance criteria are fully met with no remaining FRAC-19 blocker.
